Every component in the kit, grouped by what it does.

MeowUI ships 40+ components. They all follow the same conventions: sizes are
`'sm' | 'md' | 'lg'` resolved through `theme.metrics`, colorful intent comes
from the `Tone` union (`'primary' | 'success' | 'warning' | 'error' | 'info'`),
and every interactive component is built on the same `Pressable` foundation.

## Conventions you can rely on

- **Sizes**: `'sm' | 'md' | 'lg'` everywhere, driven by `theme.metrics`.
- **Tones**: one union for intent, resolved against `theme.colors`.
- **Icons**: pass any element to `icon` props, or register a renderer for the
  `Icon` adapter — see [Icons](/concepts/icons/).
- **Press feedback**: tint or opacity dip only. No scale, no springs.
- **Disabled states**: muted colors, not opacity hacks on colored fills.
- **Portals**: floating components stack by `theme.zIndex` — see
  [Portals & overlays](/concepts/portals/).
A quiet indeterminate spinner for brief, unmeasured waits.

import { LinkCard } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';

ActivityIndicator is a full-radius ring whose top arc carries the accent
color, spinning on a native-driven 0-360 degree rotation. Use it for waits
you cannot measure. When the fraction complete is known, use a
[ProgressBar](/components/progress-bar/) instead; when the shape of the
loading content is known, sketch it with [skeletons](/components/skeleton/).

## Import

```tsx
import { ActivityIndicator } from 'react-native-meowui';
```

## Usage

```tsx
<ActivityIndicator />

<ActivityIndicator size="lg" />

// Size the wrapper to reserve layout space, so nothing shifts
// when the spinner disappears
<ActivityIndicator style={{ width: 24, height: 24 }} />
```

## Sizes

| Size | Ring diameter |
| --- | --- |
| `sm` | 16dp |
| `md` | 20dp |
| `lg` | 24dp |

The arc is 2dp wide on `sm` and 2.5dp on the larger sizes. The rotation is a
linear native-driven loop, so the spinner keeps turning on the UI thread even
while the JS thread is busy.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `size` | `'sm' \| 'md' \| 'lg'` | `'md'` | Ring diameter. |
| `color` | `string` | `colors.primary` | Arc color. |
| `style` | `StyleProp<ViewStyle>` | — | Style for the wrapper `View`. Size it (e.g. `width`/`height`) to reserve layout space — the ring is centered inside it. |
| `testID` | `string` | — | Test identifier. |

## Accessibility

The spinner renders a plain view with no accessible role or label. Announce
the loading state on the surrounding UI instead — a labeled container or a
live region — and reserve space with `style` so the layout does not shift
when the spinner unmounts.

The kit's top bar — a 56px Surface composed from back, content and action slots.

import { LinkCard } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';

`Appbar` is the top bar of a screen: a 56px `Surface` with square corners.
Compose it from three slots — `AppbarBackAction`, `AppbarContent` and
`AppbarAction`. There is no navigation prop; the consumer owns routing.

## Import

```tsx
import { Appbar, AppbarContent, AppbarAction, AppbarBackAction } from 'react-native-meowui';
```

## Usage

```tsx
<Appbar>
  <AppbarBackAction onPress={goBack} />
  <AppbarContent title="Inbox" subtitle="3 unread" />
  <AppbarAction icon={<Icon name="search" />} onPress={openSearch} accessibilityLabel="Search" />
  <AppbarAction icon={<Icon name="ellipsis-vertical" />} onPress={openMenu} accessibilityLabel="More options" />
</Appbar>
```

```tsx
// A title-only bar without navigation.
<Appbar>
  <AppbarContent title="Settings" />
</Appbar>
```

## Composition

| Slot | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `AppbarBackAction` | Navigation back — renders a built-in chevron-left glyph. |
| `AppbarContent` | Flexible title block; takes all remaining horizontal space. |
| `AppbarAction` | Compact icon action; wraps a ghost `IconButton` at `sm` size. |

## Behavior

- The bar is a 56px `Surface` with `radius="none"`.
- `AppbarContent` flexes between its neighbors; the title and subtitle each
  clamp to one line.
- `AppbarAction` and `AppbarBackAction` inject the resolved `color` and `size`
  into icon elements that accept them, so actions stay consistent without
  manual styling.

## Props

### Appbar props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `children` | `ReactNode` | — | Bar content, usually the slot components. |
| `elevation` | `0 \| 1 \| 2` | `0` | Shadow depth. Toolbars usually stay at `0` or `1`. |
| `style` | `StyleProp<ViewStyle>` | — | Container style overrides. |
| `testID` | `string` | — | Test identifier. |

### AppbarContent props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `title` | `string` | — | Required. Title line, clamped to one row. |
| `subtitle` | `string` | — | Optional secondary line under the title. |
| `leading` | `ReactNode` | — | Leading content before the title column (rare — back actions usually sit outside). |
| `style` | `StyleProp<ViewStyle>` | — | Container style overrides. |
| `testID` | `string` | — | Test identifier. |

### AppbarAction props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `icon` | `ReactNode` | — | Required. Icon content — resolved `color` and `size` are injected when supported. |
| `onPress` | `() => void` | — | Press handler. |
| `accessibilityLabel` | `string` | — | Accessible name. Required when the icon alone is ambiguous. |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | `false` | Disables the action. |
| `testID` | `string` | — | Test identifier. |

### AppbarBackAction props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `onPress` | `() => void` | — | Press handler. |
| `accessibilityLabel` | `string` | `'Back'` | Accessible name. |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | `false` | Disables the action. |
| `testID` | `string` | — | Test identifier. |

## Accessibility

`AppbarAction` and `AppbarBackAction` wrap ghost `IconButton`s, so both are
role `button` press targets. `AppbarBackAction` announces as `Back` by default.
Give every `AppbarAction` an `accessibilityLabel` — icon-only actions have no
text fallback.

A person or entity marker with an image or a quiet initials fallback.

import { LinkCard } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';

Avatars mark people and entities. Give it an image `src`, or just a `label` and
it renders initials on a muted accent fill. One component covers lists, headers
and card leading slots.

## Import

```tsx
import { Avatar } from 'react-native-meowui';
```

## Usage

```tsx
// Initials fallback — first letters of the first two words.
<Avatar label="Ada Lovelace" />

// Explicit pixel size overrides the preset.
<Avatar label="Ada Lovelace" size={56} />

// Image fills the box; label still names it for accessibility.
<Avatar src={require('./ada.png')} label="Ada Lovelace" />

// Square-ish variant for non-person markers.
<Avatar label="ACME" radius="sm" />
```

## Sizes

| Preset | Box (px) |
| --- | --- |
| `xs` | 24 |
| `sm` | 32 |
| `md` (default) | 40 |
| `lg` | 48 |
| `xl` | 64 |

Initials scale with the box — about 40% of its size — and stay on one line.

## Behavior

- When `src` is set, the image fills the box with cover resizing; the container
  clips to the `radius` token.
- Without `src`, initials render from `label`: first letters of the first two
  words, uppercased. `ada lovelace` becomes `AL`.
- The initials fill defaults to `colors.primaryMuted`; override with
  `backgroundColor` and `textColor`.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `size` | `'xs' \| 'sm' \| 'md' \| 'lg' \| 'xl' \| number` | `'md'` (40) | Named size token or an explicit pixel size. |
| `src` | `ImageProps['source']` | — | Image source. When set, the image fills the box; otherwise initials render. |
| `label` | `string` | — | Name or label. Drives the initials fallback (first letters of the first two words, uppercased) and the accessibility label. |
| `backgroundColor` | `string` | `colors.primaryMuted` | Fill color for the initials shape. |
| `textColor` | `string` | `colors.onPrimaryMuted` | Initials color. |
| `radius` | `RadiusKey` | `'full'` | Corner radius token. |
| `style` | `StyleProp<ViewStyle>` | — | Container style overrides. |
| `testID` | `string` | — | Test identifier. |

## Accessibility

With `src`, the avatar takes role `image` and is announced by `label`. Without
an image there is no role; `label` is still applied as the accessibility label.

A small status marker — a bare dot or a count clamped at a maximum.

import { LinkCard } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';

Badge is a small pill or dot that marks a host element — an icon, a tab, an
avatar — with a count or a presence signal. It renders a dot when `content`
is omitted, and numeric content clamps at `max`: a count of 150 with the
default maximum shows `99+`. The badge sizes itself to its content, so
position it absolutely from the consumer.

## Import

```tsx
import { Badge } from 'react-native-meowui';
```

## Usage

```tsx
// A bare dot pinned to an icon — position it from the consumer
<View>
  <IconButton icon="inbox" />
  <Badge style={{ position: 'absolute', top: -2, right: -4 }} />
</View>

// Counts, clamped at `max`
<Badge content={3} tone="primary" />
<Badge content={150} />

// A zero count renders nothing unless asked otherwise
<Badge content={0} />
<Badge content={0} showZero />
```

## Dot and count

| Content | Renders |
| --- | --- |
| Omitted | A bare dot — 8dp at `md`, 6dp at `sm` |
| Number | A count pill that clamps to `N+` past `max` |
| String | The string as given |
| `0` | Nothing, unless `showZero` is set |

The default tone is `error` — the classic unread red. `neutral` inverts onto
the gray ramp: the subtle content color becomes the fill and the surface
color becomes the text on top of it.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `content` | `string \| number` | — | Text or number to display. Omit for a bare dot. |
| `tone` | `Tone` | `'error'` | Semantic color family — `neutral`, `primary`, `success`, `warning`, `error` or `info`. |
| `showZero` | `boolean` | `false` | Render the badge when the numeric content is `0`. |
| `max` | `number` | `99` | Largest count rendered before clamping to `N+`. |
| `size` | `'sm' \| 'md'` | `'md'` | Dot diameter and count height. |
| `style` | `StyleProp<ViewStyle>` | — | Style overrides. |
| `testID` | `string` | — | Test identifier. |

## Accessibility

The badge renders a plain view with no role; screen readers reach its text as
static content, detached from the control it decorates. Fold the count into
the host's `accessibilityLabel` instead — "Inbox, 3 unread" reads better than
a stray "3".

An inline announcement strip for persistent, non-blocking messages.

import { LinkCard } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';

Banner is an inline strip on an outlined surface for messages that should
stay put — an update notice, a storage warning, a maintenance note. It does
not interrupt or float; it sits in the layout until you hide it. While
`visible` is false it renders nothing, and dismissal is fully the
consumer's job — wire it through an entry in `actions` that flips `visible`.

## Import

```tsx
import { Banner } from 'react-native-meowui';
```

## Usage

```tsx
function UpdateNotice() {
  const [visible, setVisible] = useState(true);

  return (
    <Banner
      visible={visible}
      icon={<Icon name="info" />}
      text="A new version is available."
      tone="info"
      actions={[
        { label: 'Update', onPress: () => installUpdate() },
        { label: 'Dismiss', onPress: () => setVisible(false) },
      ]}
    />
  );
}
```

## Tones

| Tone | Reads as |
| --- | --- |
| `neutral` | Normal content — the default text color |
| `info`, `warning`, `error`, `success` | The tone's solid accent on message, icon and actions |

`neutral` banners read as ordinary content, which suits housekeeping notes.
The semantic tones color the message, the cloned icon and the action labels
alike, so the strip reads as one voice.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `visible` | `boolean` | — | Renders nothing while false — visibility is fully consumer-controlled. |
| `icon` | `ReactNode` | — | Leading icon content; cloned with the tone color when it accepts one. |
| `text` | `string` | — | Message body. |
| `tone` | `'neutral' \| 'info' \| 'warning' \| 'error' \| 'success'` | `'neutral'` | Color family for message, icon and actions. |
| `actions` | `BannerAction[]` | — | Ghost text buttons rendered after the message. |
| `style` | `StyleProp<ViewStyle>` | — | Style overrides for the surface. |
| `testID` | `string` | — | Test identifier. |

Each action is `{ label, onPress }`; the label doubles as the button's
accessible name.

## Accessibility

The message reads as body text, and each action renders with role `button`
labeled by its `label`. The banner is persistent and inline, so it applies no
live region — place it where readers encounter it naturally. For transient,
time-limited confirmations use [Snackbar](/components/snackbar/) instead.

An elevated bottom bar of icon destinations with optional badges.

import { LinkCard } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';

`BottomNavigation` is the app-level destination bar: a 64px, square-cornered,
elevated `Surface` whose items pair an icon with a label and an optional badge.
The consumer owns the selected state and the screens being switched.

## Import

```tsx
import { BottomNavigation } from 'react-native-meowui';
```

## Usage

```tsx
const [tab, setTab] = useState('home');

<BottomNavigation
  items={[
    { value: 'home', label: 'Home', icon: <Icon name="home" /> },
    { value: 'search', label: 'Search', icon: <Icon name="search" /> },
    { value: 'inbox', label: 'Inbox', icon: <Icon name="mail" />, badge: 3 },
    { value: 'profile', label: 'Profile', icon: <Icon name="person" /> },
  ]}
  value={tab}
  onChange={setTab}
/>
```

## Safe areas

The bar does not handle device safe areas for you. Pad it with `style` so
items clear the bottom inset and the home indicator.

```tsx
const insets = useSafeAreaInsets();

<BottomNavigation
  style={{ paddingBottom: insets.bottom }}
  items={items}
  value={tab}
  onChange={setTab}
/>
```

## Behavior

- Active icons and labels take `colors.primary`; inactive ones stay muted.
  Icons receive the resolved `color` when they accept one.
- `badge` renders a small error-colored pill on the icon's top-right — a count
  or short text.
- The bar is a `Surface` at elevation `1` with `radius="none"`; items stretch
  evenly across the width.

## Props

### BottomNavigation props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `items` | `BottomNavigationItem[]` | — | Required. Destination descriptors. |
| `value` | `string` | — | Required. The selected destination's `value`. |
| `onChange` | `(value: string) => void` | — | Required. Called with the newly selected destination's `value`. |
| `accessibilityLabel` | `string` | — | Label for the tablist. |
| `style` | `StyleProp<ViewStyle>` | — | Container style overrides; add safe-area padding here. |
| `testID` | `string` | — | Test identifier; each item appends its `value`. |

### BottomNavigationItem props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `value` | `string` | — | Required. Stable identifier reported through `onChange`. |
| `label` | `string` | — | Required. Label under the icon. |
| `icon` | `ReactNode` | — | Required. Icon content — resolved `color` is injected when supported. |
| `badge` | `number \| string` | — | Optional count or short text rendered as a pill on the icon's top-right. |

## Accessibility

The bar is role `tablist`, labelled by `accessibilityLabel`. Each item is role
`tab` with `accessibilityState` `{ selected }`, announced by its `label`. The
badge is part of the icon, not the accessible name — fold a count into the
`label` when it matters for screen readers.

A Surface docked to the bottom edge that slides up from its own measured height.

import { LinkCard } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';

`BottomSheet` presents secondary content — filters, pickers, quick actions —
without leaving the current screen. A fading scrim covers the page, and a
`Surface` with rounded top corners docks to the bottom edge, capped at 85% of
the viewport height. It slides up from its own measured height.

## Import

```tsx
import { BottomSheet } from 'react-native-meowui';
```

## Usage

Gate presentation with `visible`, and keep the component mounted while it
animates out:

```tsx
import { useState } from 'react';
import { BottomSheet, Button, Text } from 'react-native-meowui';

function FiltersSheet() {
  const [visible, setVisible] = useState(false);

  return (
    <>
      <Button variant="outline" onPress={() => setVisible(true)}>
        Filters
      </Button>

      <BottomSheet
        visible={visible}
        onDismiss={() => setVisible(false)}
        title="Filters"
      >
        <Text>Filter controls go here.</Text>
        <Button onPress={() => setVisible(false)}>Apply</Button>
      </BottomSheet>
    </>
  );
}
```

## The handle

With `handle` (the default) a 32x4 grab bar renders above the content,
centered. It is a press-to-dismiss control, not a drag gesture — tapping it
calls `onDismiss` when `dismissable` is true, exactly like tapping the scrim.

## Animation

The slide distance is the sheet's own measured height: an `onLayout` pass
measures the surface, and the sheet translates between that height and 0.
Until the first layout pass lands the sheet is kept transparent, so it never
flashes in place at full height.

Children stay mounted during the close animation and are removed only when it
finishes — state inside the sheet survives a close/reopen cycle.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `visible` | `boolean` | — | Drives presentation; keep rendering the component so it can animate out. |
| `onDismiss` | `() => void` | — | Called on scrim tap and handle tap (when `dismissable`). |
| `children` | `ReactNode` | — | Sheet content, rendered inside the surface. |
| `title` | `string` | — | Optional centered title under the handle. |
| `handle` | `boolean` | `true` | Shows the 32x4 grab bar; tapping it dismisses. |
| `dismissable` | `boolean` | `true` | Whether the scrim and handle dismiss. |
| `style` | `StyleProp<ViewStyle>` | — | Style overrides for the sheet surface. |
| `contentContainerStyle` | `StyleProp<ViewStyle>` | — | Style overrides for the animated fullscreen layer around the surface. |
| `testID` | `string` | — | Test identifier. |

## Accessibility

Both ways out are labeled buttons — the scrim and the handle, each announced
as "Dismiss sheet" and disabled while the sheet is closed or not dismissable.
The sheet surface sets `accessibilityViewIsModal`, so screen readers treat it
as its own region.

The kit's primary action — four quiet shapes across five semantic tones.

import { LinkCard } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';

Buttons communicate the main things a screen can do. MeowUI's four variants
map to a strict emphasis hierarchy, so screens stay calm without each app
reinventing its own hierarchy: **one solid button per view, tonal for
supporting actions, outline for secondary, ghost for inline emphasis**.

## Import

```tsx
import { Button } from 'react-native-meowui';
```

## Usage

```tsx
<Button onPress={save}>Save changes</Button>

<Button variant="tonal" tone="success">Approve</Button>
<Button variant="outline">Learn more</Button>
<Button variant="ghost" tone="error">Remove</Button>

<Button loading>Processing</Button>
<Button disabled>Unavailable</Button>

<Button icon={<Icon name="add" />} onPress={create}>
  New report
</Button>
```

## Variants

| Variant | Fill | Use for |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `solid` | tone fill, `on*` content | The primary action of a view |
| `tonal` | tone muted fill | Supporting actions with color weight |
| `outline` | transparent + 1px border | Secondary actions |
| `ghost` | transparent | Low-emphasis inline actions |

The `tone` prop selects the color family — `'primary'` (default), `'success'`,
`'warning'`, `'error'`, `'info'`. Disabled buttons render in the neutral
muted state regardless of tone.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `children` | `ReactNode` | — | Label text, or custom content for full control. |
| `variant` | `'solid' \| 'tonal' \| 'outline' \| 'ghost'` | `'solid'` | Visual shape. |
| `size` | `'sm' \| 'md' \| 'lg'` | `'md'` | Height from `theme.metrics.control`. |
| `tone` | `ButtonTone` | `'primary'` | Semantic color family. |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | `false` | Disables interaction, renders muted. |
| `loading` | `boolean` | `false` | Leading spinner, disables interaction. |
| `icon` | `ReactNode` | — | Leading content. Receives the resolved content `color`. |
| `trailingIcon` | `ReactNode` | — | Trailing content, colored like `icon`. |
| `fullWidth` | `boolean` | `false` | Stretch to the parent's width. |
| `onPress` | `() => void` | — | Press handler. |
| `onLongPress` | `() => void` | — | Long-press handler. |
| `accessibilityLabel` | `string` | string children | Accessible name. |
| `testID` | `string` | — | Test identifier. |
| `style` | `StyleProp<ViewStyle>` | — | Container style overrides. |
| `labelStyle` | `StyleProp<TextStyle>` | — | Label style overrides. |

## Accessibility

Role `button` with `accessibilityState` `{ disabled, busy }`. The accessible
name falls back to string children; pass `accessibilityLabel` for custom

```tsx
    </Text>

    <Button variant="ghost">Details</Button>
```

variants with distinct jobs: `assist` nudges toward an action, `filter`
toggles selection, `input` represents a value that can be removed.

## Import

```tsx
import { Chip } from 'react-native-meowui';
```

## Usage

```tsx
<Chip label="Add to list" onPress={add} />

<Chip
  variant="filter"
  label="Vegetarian"
  selected={filters.vegetarian}
  onPress={() => toggle('vegetarian')}
/>

<Chip
  variant="input"
  label="Design"
  onClose={() => remove('Design')}
/>
```

A filter row with state:

```tsx
function Filters() {
  const [active, setActive] = useState<string[]>([]);

  return (
    <View style={{ flexDirection: 'row', flexWrap: 'wrap', gap: 8 }}>
      {OPTIONS.map((option) => (
        <Chip
          key={option}
          variant="filter"
          label={option}
          selected={active.includes(option)}
          onPress={() =>
            setActive((prev) =>
              prev.includes(option)
                ? prev.filter((v) => v !== option)
                : [...prev, option]
            )
          }
        />
      ))}
    </View>
  );
}
```

## Variants

| Variant | At rest | Selected | Press calls |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `assist` | surface fill, 1px outline | — (selection ignored) | `onPress` |
| `filter` | surface fill | tone muted fill, built-in check | `onPress` |
| `input` | muted surface fill | tone muted fill | `onClose` |

- Only `assist` draws a visible border. Filter and input communicate state
  through fill alone.
- `filter` shows the built-in check glyph when selected — unless you pass
  your own `icon`, which replaces it.
- `input` is only pressable when `onClose` is provided; without it the chip
  renders disabled. The built-in close glyph appears with the handler.

Reveals or hides children by animating their measured height.

import { LinkCard } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';

`Collapsible` shows and hides content with a height animation. It is fully
controlled — you pass `expanded` and own the state. The content stays mounted
while collapsed, absolutely positioned inside the clipping box, so measurement
survives collapse and height changes re-animate.

## Import

```tsx
import { Collapsible } from 'react-native-meowui';
```

## Usage

```tsx
const [open, setOpen] = useState(false);

<View style={{ gap: 8 }}>
  <Button variant="ghost" onPress={() => setOpen((v) => !v)}>
    {open ? 'Hide details' : 'Show details'}
  </Button>
  <Collapsible expanded={open}>
    <Text variant="body">
      Extended descriptions, secondary rows, anything that should fold away.
    </Text>
  </Collapsible>
</View>
```

There is no built-in trigger. Pair it with a `Button`, a `ListItem` or any
pressable and wire its state yourself.

## Behavior

- The wrapper animates its height to the content's measured height, timed with
  `motion.durationBase` and an ease-out curve.
- The height animation runs on the **JS driver** — a documented exception in
  the kit. Height is a layout property and React Native's native driver only
  supports opacity and transforms. The animated tree here is small, which
  keeps JS-driven timing smooth.
- Collapsed content receives no touches and is excluded from the accessibility
  tree; expanding restores both.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `expanded` | `boolean` | — | Required. Whether the content is visible. |
| `children` | `ReactNode` | — | Required. Content revealed when expanded. |
| `style` | `StyleProp<ViewStyle>` | — | Container style overrides. |
| `testID` | `string` | — | Test identifier. |

## Accessibility

Collapsed content is hidden from assistive technology:
`accessibilityElementsHidden` on iOS and
`importantForAccessibility="no-hide-descendants"` on Android. Expanding
restores normal visibility. Announce the state change from your own trigger —
for rows that expand in place with that wiring built in, use `ListAccordion`.

```tsx
import { DataTable, DataTableHeader, DataTableCell, DataTableRow, DataTablePagination } from 'react-native-meowui';
```

```tsx
const [page, setPage] = useState(1);
const [selected, setSelected] = useState<string[]>([]);

  setSelected((prev) =>

    <DataTableCell>Team</DataTableCell>
    <DataTableCell numeric>Points</DataTableCell>
  </DataTableHeader>
  {pageRows.map((row) => (
    <DataTableRow
      key={row.id}
      onPress={() => toggle(row.id)}
      selected={selected.includes(row.id)}
    >
      <DataTableCell width={48} flex={0}>{row.rank}</DataTableCell>
      <DataTableCell>{row.name}</DataTableCell>
      <DataTableCell numeric>{row.points}</DataTableCell>
    </DataTableRow>

  <DataTablePagination
    page={page}
    numberOfPages={totalPages}
    onPageChange={setPage}
    label={`${rangeStart}–${rangeEnd} of ${totalRows}`}
```

import { LinkCard } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';

`Dialog` asks for a decision the rest of the screen waits on. It renders
through a portal: a fading scrim, then a centered `Surface` (elevation 3,
`lg` radius, 86% of the viewport width capped at 400) with an optional title,
a body and right-aligned actions. `AlertDialog` builds on it with the
confirmation boilerplate — title, message, Cancel and Confirm.

## Import

```tsx
import { Dialog, AlertDialog } from 'react-native-meowui';
```

## Usage

Gate presentation with `visible`, and keep the component mounted while it
animates out — do not unmount it when `visible` flips to `false`:

```tsx
import { useState } from 'react';
import { Button, Dialog, Text } from 'react-native-meowui';

function SignOutDialog() {
  const [visible, setVisible] = useState(false);

  return (
    <>
      <Button tone="error" onPress={() => setVisible(true)}>
        Sign out
      </Button>

      <Dialog
        visible={visible}
        onDismiss={() => setVisible(false)}
        title="Sign out?"
        actions={
          <>
            <Button variant="ghost" onPress={() => setVisible(false)}>
              Cancel
            </Button>
            <Button tone="error" onPress={signOut}>
              Sign out
            </Button>
          </>
        }
      >
        <Text>You will need to sign in again to keep editing.</Text>
      </Dialog>
    </>
  );
}
```

## Actions

Body content renders in a column gapped by `spacing[3]`. The `actions` prop
renders right-aligned underneath, in a row gapped by `spacing[2]`. The
convention is a ghost cancel beside a single solid confirm.

## AlertDialog

`AlertDialog` is a `Dialog` with the actions wired up: a ghost Cancel and a
solid Confirm. Confirming calls `onConfirm`, then dismisses. Pass
`tone="error"` for destructive confirmations.

```tsx
<AlertDialog
  visible={visible}
  onDismiss={() => setVisible(false)}
  title="Delete project?"
  message="This removes the project and everything in it."
  confirmLabel="Delete"
  tone="error"
  onConfirm={deleteProject}
/>
```

By default the AlertDialog scrim does not dismiss — confirmations want an
explicit choice. Pass an empty string to `cancelLabel` to hide the cancel
button.

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `visible` | `boolean` | — | Drives presentation; keep rendering the component so it can animate out. |
| `onDismiss` | `() => void` | — | Called when the scrim is tapped (and `dismissable` is true). |
| `title` | `string` | — | Title shown above the body. |
| `children` | `ReactNode` | — | Body content, rendered as-is in a `spacing[3]`-gapped column. |
| `actions` | `ReactNode` | — | Actions, rendered right-aligned in a `spacing[2]`-gapped row. |
| `dismissable` | `boolean` | `true` | Whether tapping the scrim dismisses. |
| `style` | `StyleProp<ViewStyle>` | — | Style overrides for the surface. |
| `contentContainerStyle` | `StyleProp<ViewStyle>` | — | Style overrides for the animated fullscreen layer around the surface. |
| `testID` | `string` | — | Test identifier. |

| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `visible` | `boolean` | — | Drives presentation; keep rendering the component so it can animate out. |

- `badge` renders a trailing pill — `primaryActive` fill on active rows,

  icon definition works in both states.

Floating action button, alone or expanding into a labeled action stack with a scrim.

`FAB` is a rounded-square emphasis element for the single most important
action on a screen. It fills with `primary` and is pinned by the consumer
via `style` — typically `position: 'absolute'` — so placement stays in
your hands. Pass `label` for the extended shape.

`FABGroup` wraps a FAB that expands into a labeled action stack with a
light scrim behind it. It renders through a `Portal`, so it can be mounted
anywhere and always floats above app content.

## Import

```tsx
import { FAB, FABGroup } from 'react-native-meowui';
```

## Usage

A plain FAB pinned to the bottom corner:

```tsx
<FAB
  icon={<Icon name="add" />}
  style={{ position: 'absolute', bottom: 16, right: 16 }}
  onPress={create}
/>
```

An extended FAB — pass `label`:

```tsx
<FAB
  icon={<Icon name="add" />}
  label="New report"
  style={{ position: 'absolute', bottom: 16, right: 16 }}
  onPress={create}
/>
```

A group that expands into actions:

```tsx
<FABGroup
  icon={<Icon name="add" />}
  actions={[
    { icon: <Icon name="camera" />, label: 'Scan', onPress: scan },
    { icon: <Icon name="create" />, label: 'Draft', onPress: draft },
  ]}
/>
```

Control it externally by passing `open` — without it the group manages its
own visibility and reports changes through `onOpenChange`.

## Sizes

FAB boxes are larger than control metrics by design:

| Size | Box |
| --- | --- |
| `sm` | 40 |
| `md` | 52 |
| `lg` | 60 |

The icon is 45% of the box, rounded. Extended FABs render the label at 13
(`sm`) or 14 points beside the icon.

## FABGroup behavior

- The scrim fades in from `colors.scrim`; tapping it closes the group.
- The anchor icon rotates 45 degrees while open.
- Actions fade and slide up 12 points over `motion.durationBase`.
- Each action renders as a 42-point circular surface with an elevation-2
  shadow, its label in an inverted pill beside it.
- The whole layer stacks at `theme.zIndex.menu`.

| `label` | `string` | — | When set, renders an extended FAB with the label beside the icon. |
| `size` | `'sm' \| 'md' \| 'lg'` | `'md'` | Box size. |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | `false` | Disables interaction, renders muted. |
| `onPress` | `() => void` | — | Press handler. |
| `onLongPress` | `() => void` | — | Long-press handler. |
| `accessibilityLabel` | `string` | label | Accessible name. Falls back to `label`. |

| `testID` | `string` | — | Test identifier. |
| `style` | `StyleProp<ViewStyle>` | — | Container style overrides — use this to pin the button. |

Render glyphs through one app-wide renderer — register an icon font once, use it everywhere.

import { LinkCard } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';

`Icon` renders a glyph through a renderer you register once at startup.
The kit ships no icon font; instead `Icon` is a thin, theme-aware wrapper
around whatever icon set your app already uses. `setIconRenderer` sets
that renderer app-wide.

Without a registered renderer, `Icon` renders nothing and warns in
development. Components that accept `ReactNode` icons are unaffected
either way.

## Import

```tsx
import { Icon, setIconRenderer } from 'react-native-meowui';
```

## Usage

Register once at startup, before any screen renders:

```tsx
import Ionicons from '@expo/vector-icons/Ionicons';
import { setIconRenderer } from 'react-native-meowui';

setIconRenderer(Ionicons);
```

Then use it anywhere:

```tsx
<Icon name="add" />
<Icon name="close" size={16} />
<Icon name="heart" color="#E5484D" />
```

Pass `null` to remove the renderer again:

```tsx
setIconRenderer(null);
```

## The renderer contract

Any icon font or icon component works as long as it accepts these props.
`react-native-vector-icons` and `@expo/vector-icons` satisfy it out of the
box.

```tsx
interface IconRendererProps {
  name: string;
  size?: number;
  color?: string;
  style?: StyleProp<TextStyle>;
}
```

`color` defaults to `colors.onSurface`, so icons follow the theme without
per-call colors. Pass `renderer` to a single `Icon` to override the
registered default for that call.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | `string` | — | Glyph name within the registered icon set. |
| `size` | `number` | `20` | Icon size in points. |
| `color` | `string` | `colors.onSurface` | Icon color. |
| `renderer` | `IconComponent` | — | Per-call renderer override. |
| `style` | `StyleProp<TextStyle>` | — | Style forwarded to the renderer. |

## Accessibility

An icon glyph is a visual, not a control. Screen readers do not derive
meaning from it, so pair icons with text or put an `accessibilityLabel` on
the surrounding control — `IconButton` requires one for exactly this
reason.

`IconButton` is a square touch target for a single icon. It defaults to
`ghost` — the quiet option for toolbars and list rows — and reserves
`tonal` and `solid` for actions that should carry weight.

The injected sizing matters: the component resolves the icon's `color` and
`size` from its own variant and box size, so icons stay consistent without
per-call props.

```tsx
import { IconButton } from 'react-native-meowui';
```

## Usage

```tsx
<IconButton icon={<Icon name="search" />} onPress={openSearch} />
<IconButton icon={<Icon name="delete" />} tone="error" onPress={remove} />
<IconButton icon={<Icon name="notifications" />} selected onPress={toggle} />
<IconButton icon={<Icon name="add" />} variant="solid" onPress={create} />
```

A toolbar row:

```tsx
<View style={{ flexDirection: 'row', gap: 4 }}>
  <IconButton icon={<Icon name="arrow-back" />} onPress={goBack} />
  <IconButton icon={<Icon name="bookmark" />} selected />
  <IconButton icon={<Icon name="more-vert" />} onPress={showMenu} />
</View>
```

## Variants

| Variant | At rest | Pressed | Selected |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `ghost` | transparent, tone-colored icon | background tint | tonal muted fill |
| `tonal` | transparent, tone-colored icon | background tint | tonal muted fill |
| `solid` | tone fill, `on*` icon | opacity dip | — |
| `outline` | transparent with 1px border | background tint | — |

Ghost and tonal render identically — pressed state included — so the two
names carry intent, not different pixels. `selected` affects the ghost and
tonal variants only; a solid button is always filled.

Boxes come from `theme.metrics.icon`; the icon itself is 55% of the box,
rounded:

| Size | Box | Icon |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `sm` | 28 | 15 |
| `md` | 36 | 20 |
| `lg` | 44 | 24 |

row, and `ListAccordion` expands into content below its header row.

## Import

```tsx
import { ListSection, ListItem, ListAccordion } from 'react-native-meowui';
```

## Usage

```tsx
<ListSection header="Notifications">
  <ListItem
    leading={<Icon name="mail" />}
    title="Email digest"
    description="A weekly summary of account activity."
    trailing={<Switch checked={digest} onValueChange={setDigest} accessibilityLabel="Email digest" />}
  />
  <ListItem
    leading={<Icon name="notifications" />}
    title="Push notifications"
    trailing={<Switch checked={push} onValueChange={setPush} accessibilityLabel="Push notifications" />}
  />
  <ListItem title="Sign out" onPress={signOut} disabled={busy} />
</ListSection>
```

## Accordion state

`ListAccordion` works uncontrolled or controlled.

```tsx
// Uncontrolled — the accordion keeps its own state.
<ListSection header="Playback">
  <ListAccordion leading={<Icon name="options" />} title="Audio quality">
    <ListItem title="High" onPress={() => pick('high')} selected={quality === 'high'} />
    <ListItem title="Normal" onPress={() => pick('normal')} selected={quality === 'normal'} />
  </ListAccordion>
</ListSection>
```

```tsx
// Controlled — the parent owns the expanded state.
const [open, setOpen] = useState(false);

<ListAccordion
  leading={<Icon name="options" />}
  title="Audio quality"
  expanded={open}
  onExpandedChange={setOpen}
>
  <ListItem title="High" />
  <ListItem title="Normal" />
</ListAccordion>
```

- Rows press with a `surfaceMuted` tint; disabled rows mute their content
  instead of dimming.
- `selected` on a `ListItem` sets a semibold title and tints the leading icon
  with `colors.primary`.
- The accordion chevron rotates 90 degrees on the native driver; the body
  animates its measured height on the JS driver over `motion.durationBase`.
- `description` clamps to two lines. Rows without it are 56px tall; with it,
  68px minimum.

A floating action list anchored to a trigger, clamped to stay on screen.

import { LinkCard } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';

`Menu` shows a list of `MenuItem` rows in a floating `Surface` (elevation 2,
`sm` radius, hairline border) over a transparent scrim. It fades in with a
small downward settle. Position it with `anchor` — the screen coordinates of
the desired top-left corner — or omit `anchor` to center it on the viewport.

## Import

```tsx
import { Menu, MenuItem } from 'react-native-meowui';
```

## Usage

Measure the trigger with `measureInWindow` and pass the result as the anchor.
Wrap the trigger in a `View` ref — with `collapsible={false}` so the layout
node survives Android view flattening — and open the menu just below it:

```tsx
import { useRef, useState } from 'react';
import { View } from 'react-native';
import { Button, Menu, MenuItem } from 'react-native-meowui';

function RowActions() {
  const triggerRef = useRef<View>(null);
  const [anchor, setAnchor] = useState({ x: 0, y: 0 });
  const [visible, setVisible] = useState(false);

  const open = () => {
    triggerRef.current?.measureInWindow((x, y, _width, height) => {
      setAnchor({ x, y: y + height + 4 });
      setVisible(true);
    });
  };

  return (
    <View ref={triggerRef} collapsable={false}>
      <Button variant="ghost" onPress={open}>
        Options
      </Button>

      <Menu visible={visible} onDismiss={() => setVisible(false)} anchor={anchor}>
        <MenuItem label="Rename" onPress={() => setVisible(false)} />
        <MenuItem label="Duplicate" onPress={() => setVisible(false)} />
        <MenuItem label="Delete" disabled onPress={() => setVisible(false)} />
      </Menu>
    </View>
  );
}
```

## Anchoring

`anchor` is exactly what `measureInWindow` returns: screen coordinates where
the menu's top-left corner should appear. The menu keeps 8dp from the screen
edges — the x position clamps against the menu width, the y position clamps
against its measured height — so a menu near the bottom or right edge shifts
into view instead of clipping. The vertical clamp needs the measured height,
so on the first frame a menu anchored near the bottom edge may sit one frame
low.

## Menu items

`MenuItem` rows are at least 44pt tall with a muted pressed tint. They take
optional `leading` and `trailing` content, and a `selected` state that
renders a built-in check glyph when no `leading` is given:

```tsx
<Menu visible={visible} onDismiss={close} anchor={anchor}>
  <MenuItem label="Ascending" selected={sort === 'asc'} onPress={() => setSort('asc')} />
  <MenuItem label="Descending" selected={sort === 'desc'} onPress={() => setSort('desc')} />
  <MenuItem label="Custom" leading={<Icon name="edit" />} onPress={openCustom} />
</Menu>
```

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `visible` | `boolean` | — | Drives presentation; keep rendering the component so it can animate out. |
| `onDismiss` | `() => void` | — | Called when the scrim closes the menu. |
| `anchor` | `{ x: number; y: number }` | — | Screen coordinates (e.g. from `measureInWindow`) where the menu's top-left corner should appear, clamped to stay on screen. Omit to center the menu on the viewport. |
| `width` | `number` | `200` | Menu width in dp. |
| `children` | `ReactNode` | — | Menu content — usually `MenuItem` rows. |
| `dismissable` | `boolean` | `true` | Whether the transparent scrim closes the menu. |
| `style` | `StyleProp<ViewStyle>` | — | Style overrides for the menu surface. |
| `testID` | `string` | — | Test identifier. |

## MenuItem props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `leading` | `ReactNode` | — | Leading content; when omitted and `selected`, a check glyph is shown. |
| `label` | `string` | — | Row label; also the accessible name. |
| `trailing` | `ReactNode` | — | Trailing content. |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | `false` | Disables the row. |
| `onPress` | `() => void` | — | Press handler. |
| `selected` | `boolean` | `false` | Marks the row selected; shows a check glyph when no `leading` is given. |
| `style` | `StyleProp<ViewStyle>` | — | Style overrides for the row. |
| `testID` | `string` | — | Test identifier. |

## Accessibility

The transparent scrim is a labeled button ("Close menu"). Each row has role
`menuitem`, its `label` as the accessible name, and an `accessibilityState`
of `{ disabled, checked }` — `checked` is set when the row is `selected`.

A fullscreen scrim with no imposed layout — you place your own Surface.

import { LinkCard } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';

`Modal` is the generic overlay the kit's dialogs are built from: a fading
scrim plus a fullscreen animated layer you fill freely. Unlike `Dialog`, no
`Surface` is imposed. The layer around your content is fullscreen with
`box-none` pointer events, so placement is entirely yours. It fades and
scales in (0.96 to 1) exactly like a dialog.

## Import

```tsx
import { Modal } from 'react-native-meowui';
```

## Usage

Gate presentation with `visible`, and keep the component mounted while it
animates out:

```tsx
import { useState } from 'react';
import { Modal, Surface, Text } from 'react-native-meowui';

function Spotlight() {
  const [visible, setVisible] = useState(false);

  return (
    <Modal visible={visible} onDismiss={() => setVisible(false)}>
      <Surface
        elevation={3}
        radius="lg"
        style={{ position: 'absolute', top: '30%', left: 24, right: 24 }}
      >
        <Text>Anything can live here.</Text>
      </Surface>
    </Modal>
  );
}
```

## Positioning

The children layer covers the screen but lets touches through to nothing
except your content, so position it yourself — usually an
absolutely-positioned `Surface`:

```tsx
<Modal visible={visible} onDismiss={() => setVisible(false)}>
  <Surface
    elevation={3}
    radius="lg"
    style={{ position: 'absolute', bottom: 24, left: 24, right: 24 }}
  >
    <Text>This panel hugs the bottom edge, 24 in from the sides.</Text>
  </Surface>
</Modal>
```

`onDismiss` is optional. When it is omitted the scrim becomes inert — useful
for blocking flows that need an explicit choice inside the modal.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `visible` | `boolean` | — | Drives presentation; keep rendering the component so it can animate out. |
| `onDismiss` | `() => void` | — | Called when the scrim is tapped and `dismissable` is true. |
| `dismissable` | `boolean` | `true` | Whether tapping the scrim dismisses. |
| `children` | `ReactNode` | — | Full control over the contents — usually an absolutely-positioned `Surface`. The layer around them is fullscreen (`box-none`), so you choose the placement. |
| `contentContainerStyle` | `StyleProp<ViewStyle>` | — | Style overrides for the fullscreen animated layer wrapping `children`. |
| `style` | `StyleProp<ViewStyle>` | — | Style overrides for the outer fullscreen layer. |
| `testID` | `string` | — | Test identifier. |

## Accessibility

The scrim is a labeled button ("Dismiss") that disables itself while the
modal is closed, not dismissable, or missing `onDismiss`. The content layer
turns its pointer events off while closed. Modal sets no
`accessibilityViewIsModal` itself — add it to your own surface when it should
act as a modal region for screen readers.

import { LinkCard } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';

`Portal` teleports children to the nearest `PortalHost` above the
surrounding tree. Content keeps rendering — and re-rendering — normally;
only its position in the hierarchy changes. That is what lets menus,
dialogs and toasts escape clipped or stacked parents. `PortalHost` is the
mount point that renders that content above its own children.

`<MeowProvider>` already includes a host, so most apps never mount one
directly. Nest additional hosts when content must layer inside a specific
region, such as a modal.

## Import

```tsx
import { Portal, PortalHost } from 'react-native-meowui';
```

## Usage

A badge that floats above its parent's clipping:

```tsx
<View style={{ overflow: 'hidden' }}>
  <Portal zIndex={900}>
    <Text>Rendered in the host's overlay, not here</Text>
  </Portal>
</View>
```

An extra host scoped to a modal, so portaled content stays inside it:

```tsx
<PortalHost>
  <MyModalContent />
</PortalHost>
```

If a `Portal` renders without a host above it, it renders nothing and
warns in development. Restoring `<MeowProvider>` — or mounting a
`<PortalHost>` — fixes it.

## Stacking

Entries sort by `zIndex`; ties keep mount order. Pass a token from
`theme.zIndex` (`sticky`, `menu`, `sheet`, `dialog`, `toast`, `tooltip`) so
overlapping overlays stack by token instead of mount order:

```tsx
<Portal zIndex={zIndex.menu}>   {/* 900 */}
<Portal zIndex={zIndex.toast}>  {/* 1050 — renders above the menu */}
```

## Props

### Portal

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `children` | `ReactNode` | — | Content to teleport to the nearest host. |
| `zIndex` | `number` | `0` | Stacking level within the host (see `theme.zIndex`). |

### PortalHost

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `children` | `ReactNode` | — | Content rendered below the portal layer. |

## Accessibility

Portaled content ends up in the host's overlay layer, outside the
surrounding layout context. Give overlays their own roles, labels and
announcements rather than relying on surrounding headings — see the
concepts page for the full model.

The kit's touchable primitive — pressed state as a tint or an opacity dip, nothing else.

import { LinkCard } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';

`Pressable` is the kit's touchable primitive. It communicates pressed state
with a background tint or an opacity dip only — no scale, no springs — so
every interactive element in MeowUI feels the same under the finger. All
interactive kit components are built on it; reach for it directly when
composing your own controls so they match.

Feedback follows one rule:

- Pass `tint` and the pressed state fills the background with that color.
- Omit `tint` and the pressed state dips opacity to `pressedOpacity` —
  safe on any background.

A disabled pressable settles at `disabledOpacity`.

## Import

```tsx
import { Pressable } from 'react-native-meowui';
```

## Usage

```tsx
import { useRef } from 'react';
import { Pressable, Text } from 'react-native-meowui';

function Example() {
  const ref = useRef<PressableRef>(null);

  return (
    <Pressable
      ref={ref}
      tint="#00000010"
      radius="md"
      onPress={save}
    >
      <Text>Save</Text>
    </Pressable>
  );
}
```

Opacity feedback instead of a tint:

```tsx
<Pressable pressedOpacity={0.8} onPress={open}>
  <Text>Open</Text>
</Pressable>
```

`style` also accepts a render function that receives the current `pressed`
state, like React Native's `Pressable`:

```tsx
<Pressable
  style={({ pressed }) => [{ borderColor: pressed ? '#888' : '#ddd' }]}
  onPress={open}
>
  <Text>Open</Text>
</Pressable>
```

## Ref

Refs expose a `PressableRef`, a structural handle to the underlying host
view with the imperative methods you usually need:

```tsx
interface PressableRef {
  focus(options?: { preventScroll?: boolean }): void;
  blur(): void;
  measure(fn: (x: number, y: number, width: number, height: number, pageX: number, pageY: number) => void): void;
  measureInWindow(fn: (x: number, y: number, width: number, height: number) => void): void;
}
```

It is declared structurally rather than re-exporting React Native's
`HostInstance`, which aliases a compiler-private class that cannot appear
in emitted declarations.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `tint` | `string` | — | Background color applied while pressed. When omitted, pressed feedback is a subtle opacity dip — safe on any background. |
| `radius` | `RadiusKey \| number` | `'sm'` | Corner radius as a token key or explicit number. |
| `pressedOpacity` | `number` | `0.85` | Opacity applied while pressed when no `tint` is given. |
| `disabledOpacity` | `number` | `0.45` | Opacity applied when disabled. |

All other React Native `PressableProps` — `onPress`, `onLongPress`,
`disabled`, `hitSlop`, accessibility props, function `style` — pass through
unchanged.

## Accessibility

`Pressable` sets no role itself; the component you compose decides. Pass
`accessibilityRole`, `accessibilityLabel` and `accessibilityState` through
so your control is announced correctly — see `Button` and `IconButton` for
the pattern. Because feedback never moves or scales content, focus and
reading order stay stable while pressing.

A thin linear track for measurable progress, or a quiet sweep when the length is unknown.

import { LinkCard } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
import { Aside } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';

ProgressBar is a thin, fully rounded track. With a `progress` prop the fill
animates to that fraction of the measured track width; without one the bar
runs a quiet indeterminate sweep. Reach for it when work has a known length —
uploads, downloads, multi-step forms — and let [ActivityIndicator](/components/activity-indicator/)
handle the unmeasured cases.

## Import

```tsx
import { ProgressBar } from 'react-native-meowui';
```

## Usage

```tsx
function Upload() {
  const [progress, setProgress] = useState(0);

  useEffect(() => {
    const timer = setInterval(() => {
      setProgress((p) => Math.min(1, p + 0.05));
    }, 100);
    return () => clearInterval(timer);
  }, []);

  return <ProgressBar progress={progress} />;
}
```

Omit `progress` for an indeterminate sweep:

```tsx
<ProgressBar />
```

## Modes

| Mode | How | Behavior |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Determinate | Pass `progress` from 0 to 1 | The fill animates to the fraction of the measured track width. Values outside the range are clamped. |
| Indeterminate | Omit `progress` | A bar covering 30% of the track sweeps across on a 1.2s loop. |

<Aside type="note">
The determinate fill animates `width`, a layout property the native driver
cannot handle, so this one animation runs on the JS thread. The node is a
single absolutely-positioned bar and the timing is short, which keeps that
cost negligible — a transform-based width hack would distort the fill's
rounded ends.
</Aside>

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `progress` | `number` | — | Fill level from 0 to 1. Omit for an indeterminate sweep. |
| `height` | `number` | `4` | Track height in dp. |
| `color` | `string` | `colors.primary` | Fill color. |
| `trackColor` | `string` | `colors.surfaceMuted` | Track color. |
| `style` | `StyleProp<ViewStyle>` | — | Style overrides for the track. |
| `testID` | `string` | — | Test identifier. |

## Accessibility

The track takes the `progressbar` role. Determinate bars expose
`accessibilityValue` with `min: 0`, `max: 1` and the clamped `progress` as
`now`; indeterminate bars omit the value, since there is nothing to report.

Single-choice rows — standalone, or driven together by a RadioGroup.

import { LinkCard } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';

Radio is a single-choice option row. It works two ways: standalone, where you
pass `selected` and `onValueChange` directly, or inside a `RadioGroup`, which
lays the options out in a column and derives each row's checked state from the
group's value. Inside a group, each `Radio` needs a `value`; the row is
checked when its value matches, and pressing it reports that value back.
Radios without a `value` never check inside a group.

## Import

```tsx
import { Radio, RadioGroup } from 'react-native-meowui';
```

## Usage

The group is controlled: you own the selected value, and `onValueChange`
reports the tapped radio's `value`.

```tsx
const [size, setSize] = useState<string | null>('md');

<RadioGroup value={size} onValueChange={setSize}>
  <Radio label="Small" value="sm" />
  <Radio label="Medium" value="md" />
  <Radio label="Large" value="lg" />
</RadioGroup>
```

Start from `null` when nothing should be selected initially.

```tsx
const [plan, setPlan] = useState<string | null>(null);

<RadioGroup value={plan} onValueChange={setPlan}>
  <Radio label="Free" value="free" />
  <Radio label="Pro" value="pro" />
  <Radio label="Team — disabled during the beta" value="team" disabled />
</RadioGroup>
```

Standalone radios manage a single boolean-like selection and ignore the group
context (there is none).

```tsx
const [notify, setNotify] = useState(false);

<Radio
  label="Only this device"
  selected={notify}
  onValueChange={() => setNotify(!notify)}
/>
```

## RadioGroup

`RadioGroup` renders its children in a column with the theme's control gap
and owns the selection state. Only `Radio` children participate — any other
children render as-is.

## Props

### Radio

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `selected` | `boolean` | `false` | Selected state when used standalone; ignored inside a `RadioGroup`. |
| `onValueChange` | `() => void` | — | Standalone only: called when the row is pressed. |
| `value` | `string` | — | Option value — lets a `RadioGroup` drive selection for this radio. |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | `false` | Disables interaction, mutes the circle and label. |
| `label` | `ReactNode` | — | Content rendered beside the circle; the whole row is the tap target. |
| `tone` | `RadioTone` | `'primary'` | Semantic color family for the selected state. |
| `style` | `StyleProp<ViewStyle>` | — | Row style overrides. |
| `testID` | `string` | — | Test identifier. |

### RadioGroup

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `value` | `string \| null` | — | Currently selected option value; `null` when nothing is selected. |
| `onValueChange` | `(value: string) => void` | — | Called with the tapped radio's `value`. |
| `children` | `ReactNode` | — | The option rows. |
| `style` | `StyleProp<ViewStyle>` | — | Container style overrides. |

## Tones

The `tone` prop colors the selected ring and dot — `'primary'` (default),
`'success'`, `'warning'`, `'error'`, `'info'`. Unselected circles stay neutral
regardless of tone.

## Accessibility

Each row has role `radio` with `accessibilityState` `{ checked, disabled }`,
and the group container has role `radiogroup`. The row reads its visible text
content as its name, so string labels need nothing extra; with custom
`label` content, wrap or label the row yourself. Rows keep a 40pt minimum
height.

A borderless, filled search field with a built-in magnifier and clear affordance.

import { LinkCard } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';

Searchbar is a purpose-built search field. It is the one control that trades
the kit's hairline outline for a muted pill-shaped fill, so it stands apart
from form inputs on the same screen. A magnifier glyph and an optional clear
affordance are built in — no icon library required.

## Import

```tsx
import { Searchbar } from 'react-native-meowui';
```

## Usage

The field is controlled: you own the text, and `onChangeText` fires on every
change. Provide `onClear` and the clear button appears whenever the value is
non-empty.

```tsx
const [query, setQuery] = useState('');

<Searchbar
  value={query}
  onChangeText={setQuery}
  placeholder="Search notes"
  onClear={() => setQuery('')}
/>
```

`leading` replaces the built-in magnifier when you need something else in
front of the input.

```tsx
<Searchbar
  value={query}
  onChangeText={setQuery}
  leading={<Icon name="filter" />}
  placeholder="Filter by tag"
/>

<Searchbar value={query} onChangeText={setQuery} disabled placeholder="Search is offline" />
```

## Clear affordance

The clear button shows only when all three hold: `onClear` was provided, the
field is not disabled, and `value` is non-empty. It sits inside the field,
labeled "Clear search" for assistive technology, and shares the field's
`testID` with a `-clear` suffix.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `value` | `string` | — | Current text (controlled). |
| `onChangeText` | `(text: string) => void` | — | Called on every text change. |
| `placeholder` | `string` | — | Placeholder shown while the field is empty. |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | `false` | Disables editing and hides the clear affordance. |
| `onClear` | `() => void` | — | When provided and `value` is non-empty, a clear affordance is shown. |
| `leading` | `ReactNode` | — | Leading content; defaults to a built-in magnifier glyph. |
| `accessibilityLabel` | `string` | — | Names the input for assistive technology. |
| `style` | `StyleProp<ViewStyle>` | — | Field style overrides. |
| `testID` | `string` | — | Test identifier; the clear button appends `-clear`. |

## Accessibility

The input carries role `search`, and the clear affordance is a separate
button labeled "Clear search". Pass `accessibilityLabel` when the placeholder
alone does not describe the field's purpose.

A dropdown select that opens a Menu anchored below the trigger.

import { LinkCard } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';

Select is a dropdown for choosing one option from a list. The trigger is an
outlined field showing the current selection; pressing it opens a `Menu`
anchored just below. The chevron flips while the menu is open, and the chosen
item shows its selected state inside the menu.

## Import

```tsx
import { Select } from 'react-native-meowui';
```

## Usage

The component is controlled: you own the value, and `onValueChange` reports
the chosen option's `value`. Start from `null` to show the placeholder.

```tsx
const [size, setSize] = useState<string | null>(null);

<Select
  options={[
    { label: 'Small', value: 'sm' },
    { label: 'Medium', value: 'md' },
    { label: 'Large', value: 'lg' },
  ]}
  value={size}
  onValueChange={setSize}
  placeholder="Choose a size"
/>
```

Individual options can be disabled, and the `error` flag recolors the trigger
border for form validation.

```tsx
<Select
  options={[
    { label: 'Standard', value: 'standard' },
    { label: 'Express — unavailable', value: 'express', disabled: true },
  ]}
  value={shipping}
  onValueChange={setShipping}
  error
/>
```

## How it opens

On press, the trigger measures itself in window coordinates and opens the
menu anchored just below it — 4pt of breathing room, and at least 200pt wide
so short triggers still produce a readable menu. The menu is rendered through
a portal above the rest of the UI, so it is not clipped by parent views. See
[Portals](/concepts/portals/) for how that layering works and how to keep
overlays from fighting each other.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `options` | `SelectOption[]` | — | The choices, in display order. |
| `value` | `string \| null` | — | Currently selected value, or `null` for the placeholder state. |
| `onValueChange` | `(value: string) => void` | — | Called with the chosen option's `value`; the menu then closes. |
| `placeholder` | `string` | `'Select…'` | Shown when no value is selected. |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | `false` | Disables interaction, mutes the trigger. |
| `error` | `boolean` | `false` | Renders the trigger border in `colors.error`. |
| `accessibilityLabel` | `string` | — | Names the trigger; falls back to the selected label, then the placeholder. |
| `style` | `StyleProp<ViewStyle>` | — | Trigger style overrides. |
| `testID` | `string` | — | Test identifier. |

Options are plain objects:

| Field | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `label` | `string` | Text shown in the menu and on the trigger once selected. |
| `value` | `string` | Reported through `onValueChange` when chosen. |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | Grays the item out and blocks selection. |

## Accessibility

The trigger has role `button` with `accessibilityState` `{ disabled, expanded
}`, so screen readers announce whether the menu is open. Its accessible name
falls back to the selected option's label, then the placeholder; pass
`accessibilityLabel` when that is not descriptive enough. Menu item
semantics come from `Menu` itself.

import { LinkCard } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';

Skeleton is a quiet block in the muted surface color whose opacity pulses
between 0.5 and 1 on a native-driven loop. Compose several to sketch the
shape of the real content — text lines, avatars, card blocks — instead of
showing a spinner. The layout the user sees loading is the layout they get.

## Import

```tsx
import { Skeleton } from 'react-native-meowui';
```

## Usage

```tsx
function ProfileSkeleton() {
  return (
    <View style={{ padding: 16, gap: 12 }}>
      <View style={{ flexDirection: 'row', alignItems: 'center', gap: 12 }}>
        <Skeleton width={40} height={40} circle />
        <View style={{ flex: 1, gap: 6 }}>
          <Skeleton width="60%" height={16} />
          <Skeleton width="40%" height={12} />
        </View>
      </View>
      <Skeleton height={80} radius="md" />
    </View>
  );
}
```

## Shaping placeholders

| Placeholder | Recipe |
| --- | --- |
| Text line | The default 14dp height with a partial `width` |
| Avatar | `circle` — `width` collapses to `height` and the radius becomes full |
| Card or media block | A larger `height` with `radius="md"` or wider |

rather than several busy elements.

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `width` | `number \| string` | `'100%'` | Block width. |
| `height` | `number` | `14` | Block height in dp. |
| `radius` | `RadiusKey` | `'sm'` | Corner radius token. |
| `circle` | `boolean` | `false` | Force a circle: `width` collapses to `height` and the radius becomes full. |

| `testID` | `string` | — | Test identifier. |

for sighted users. Keep the wait short, and announce the loading state at a
higher level if needed, for example with a live region on the container that
swaps to the real content.

A quiet, hairline slider for picking a value from a range.

import { LinkCard } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';

Slider is a low-emphasis range control: a 4pt hairline track with a fill and
a small thumb. Tapping jumps to the touched position and dragging follows the
finger. Values always clamp to the `[min, max]` range, and snap to `step`
when one is provided.

## Import

```tsx
import { Slider } from 'react-native-meowui';
```

## Usage

The component is controlled: you own the value, and `onValueChange` fires
continuously while the user taps or drags. Without `min`, `max` and `step`
the slider runs continuously from `0` to `1`.

```tsx
const [volume, setVolume] = useState(0.5);

<Slider value={volume} onValueChange={setVolume} accessibilityLabel="Volume" />
```

With a `step`, the value snaps to increments of that size — useful for
counts and ratings. Snapped values are rounded to avoid floating-point
drift.

```tsx
const [count, setCount] = useState(20);

<Slider
  value={count}
  onValueChange={setCount}
  min={0}
  max={100}
  step={5}
  accessibilityLabel="Number of items"
/>
```

## Interaction

The container is 40pt tall, and that full height doubles as the tap and drag
area — there is no need to hit the 4pt track itself. Gestures run through a
`PanResponder` created once per component; it reads the latest `min`, `max`,
`step` and `onValueChange` through a ref rather than re-creating on every
render. On touch-down, the tap position is measured relative to the container
and emitted immediately; during the drag, movement is tracked relative to that
starting point, so the thumb follows the finger rather than chasing it. When
`disabled` is set, the responder never engages and accessibility actions are
ignored.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `value` | `number` | — | Current value. |
| `onValueChange` | `(value: number) => void` | — | Called with the next value while the user taps or drags the track. |
| `min` | `number` | `0` | Lower bound. |
| `max` | `number` | `1` | Upper bound. |
| `step` | `number` | — | Snap increment; omit for a continuous slider. |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | `false` | Disables interaction. |
| `accessibilityLabel` | `string` | — | Accessibility label — adjustable elements should describe what they set. |
| `style` | `StyleProp<ViewStyle>` | — | Container style overrides. |
| `testID` | `string` | — | Test identifier. |

## Accessibility

Role `adjustable`, with `accessibilityValue` reporting `{ min, max, now }` so
screen readers can announce the position in the range, and
`accessibilityState` `{ disabled }`. The slider exposes `increment` and
`decrement` accessibility actions: each press moves the value by `step` when
one is set, or by one hundredth of the range on a continuous slider. Since the
control communicates only through geometry, pass `accessibilityLabel`
describing what it sets.

A transient confirmation bar anchored to the bottom of the viewport, with an optional action.

import { LinkCard } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';

Snackbar is a transient confirmation bar that renders through a
[Portal](/concepts/portals/), anchored to the bottom of the viewport. It
slides up and fades in, auto-dismisses after four seconds, and keeps
animating out after `visible` flips false — so keep the component mounted
and let it own the exit. One action, such as Undo, may ride along; pressing
it dismisses the snackbar as well.

## Import

```tsx
import { Snackbar } from 'react-native-meowui';
```

## Usage

```tsx
function SaveNotice() {
  const [visible, setVisible] = useState(false);

  return (
    <View>
      <Button onPress={() => setVisible(true)}>Save report</Button>

      {/* Keep the component mounted so it can animate out */}
      <Snackbar
        visible={visible}
        message="Report saved"
        action={{ label: 'Undo', onPress: () => undoSave() }}
        onDismiss={() => setVisible(false)}
      />
    </View>
  );
}
```

## Timing and dismissal

| Event | What happens |
| --- | --- |
| Auto-dismiss | After `duration` milliseconds, `onDismiss` is called. The timer restarts when `message` changes, so a replaced notice gets a full window. |
| Action pressed | The action's `onPress` runs first, then `onDismiss`. |
| `visible` flips false | The snackbar animates out, then unmounts itself. |

`onDismiss` is your cue in every case — flip `visible` there.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `visible` | `boolean` | — | Drives presentation; keep rendering the component so it can animate out. |
| `message` | `string` | — | Message body, wrapped at two lines. |
| `action` | `SnackbarAction` | — | Single trailing action. Pressing it also dismisses the snackbar. |
| `duration` | `number` | `4000` | Milliseconds before auto-dismiss. |
| `onDismiss` | `() => void` | — | Called on auto-dismiss and after the action is pressed — flip `visible` here. |
| `style` | `StyleProp<ViewStyle>` | — | Style overrides for the surface. |
| `testID` | `string` | — | Test identifier. |

`SnackbarAction` is `{ label, onPress }`. The bar renders on the inverse
surface color, so it stays legible over any content beneath it.

## Accessibility

The surface carries `accessibilityLiveRegion="polite"`, so screen readers
announce the message when it appears. The action renders with role `button`,
labeled by its `label`.

The kit's container primitive — a themed fill with optional hairline border and elevation.

import { LinkCard } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';

`Surface` is the kit's container primitive: a themed fill with an optional
hairline border and elevation. Cards, sheets, app bars and lists are all
Surfaces, which is what keeps backgrounds, borders and shadows consistent
across a screen.

Two elevation styles exist by design. In-flow surfaces should stay at
elevation `0` and separate with a hairline border; reserved shadow depth is
for overlays such as menus, dialogs, sheets and snackbars.

## Import

```tsx
import { Surface } from 'react-native-meowui';
```

## Usage

```tsx
{/* Plain card — hairline border instead of shadow */}
<Surface outlined radius="lg" style={{ padding: 16 }}>
  <Text variant="title">Workspace</Text>
</Surface>

{/* Elevated overlay */}
<Surface elevation={2} radius="md" style={{ padding: 16 }}>
  <Text variant="body">Floating panel</Text>
</Surface>

{/* Tinted fill, e.g. a muted banner */}
<Surface backgroundColor={colors.surfaceMuted} radius="md" />
```

## Elevation

`elevation` is a closed level from `0` to `3`. Level `0` renders no shadow.
The shadow color comes from `colors.shadow`; both platform styles are
emitted together and each platform ignores the other's properties.

| Level | iOS shadow (opacity / radius / offset) | Android elevation |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `0` | none | none |
| `1` | 0.08 / 3 / (1, 1) | 2 |
| `2` | 0.1 / 6 / (0, 2) | 4 |
| `3` | 0.14 / 10 / (0, 4) | 8 |

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `elevation` | `0 \| 1 \| 2 \| 3` | `0` | Shadow depth. Overlays use 1–3; in-flow surfaces should stay at 0. |
| `outlined` | `boolean` | `false` | Draw a 1px hairline border (`colors.outline`). |
| `radius` | `'none' \| 'xs' \| 'sm' \| 'md' \| 'lg' \| 'xl' \| 'full'` | `'md'` | Corner radius token. |
| `backgroundColor` | `string` | `colors.surface` | Fill color. |
| `style` | `StyleProp<ViewStyle>` | — | Container style overrides. |

All other React Native `ViewProps` — `children`, `testID`, layout props —
pass through unchanged.

## Accessibility

`Surface` is a plain view and conveys nothing on its own. Semantics come
from the content you put inside it, so group related children here and let
the inner controls carry roles and labels.

A controlled on/off toggle with a native-driven thumb.

import { LinkCard } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';

Switch is a controlled on/off toggle. The thumb glides between ends on a
native-driven transform — only the translate is animated, on a fast
decelerating 120 ms curve — so the gesture stays smooth on low-end devices.
The off state keeps a hairline border on track and thumb so the control still
reads on white surfaces.

## Import

```tsx
import { Switch } from 'react-native-meowui';
```

## Usage

The component is controlled: you own the state, and `onValueChange` hands you
the next value.

```tsx
const [wifi, setWifi] = useState(true);

<Switch checked={wifi} onValueChange={setWifi} accessibilityLabel="Wi-Fi" />
```

Tones color the on state; a disabled switch that is on keeps a muted fill
instead of fading out.

```tsx
const [boost, setBoost] = useState(false);

<Switch
  checked={boost}
  onValueChange={setBoost}
  tone="success"
  accessibilityLabel="Performance boost"
/>

<Switch checked accessibilityLabel="Managed by policy" disabled />
```

The touch target is at least 48pt tall and stretches to the parent's width,
so the whole row area around the track toggles the switch.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `checked` | `boolean` | — | Whether the switch is on. |
| `onValueChange` | `(checked: boolean) => void` | — | Called with the next state when the switch is pressed. |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | `false` | Disables interaction. |
| `tone` | `SwitchTone` | `'primary'` | Semantic color family for the on state. |
| `accessibilityLabel` | `string` | — | Accessibility label — the control is glyph-only, so provide one. |
| `style` | `StyleProp<ViewStyle>` | — | Hit-area style overrides. |
| `testID` | `string` | — | Test identifier. |

## Tones

The `tone` prop selects the on-state fill — `'primary'` (default),
`'success'`, `'warning'`, `'error'`, `'info'`. The off state is neutral
regardless of tone.

## Accessibility

Role `switch` with `accessibilityState` `{ checked, disabled }`. The control
communicates only through its glyph, so pass `accessibilityLabel` describing
what it turns on or off.

A quiet tab bar with fixed and scrollable variants and an animated indicator.

import { LinkCard } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';

`Tabs` renders the bar only — a 48px row of tab presses with a hairline bottom
border and a 2px `primary` indicator on the active tab. The content region
below is yours to compose. Use `fixed` for a handful of tabs, `scrollable` when
labels overflow.

## Import

```tsx
import { Tabs } from 'react-native-meowui';
```

## Usage

```tsx
const [tab, setTab] = useState('all');

<Tabs
  tabs={[
    { value: 'all', label: 'All' },
    { value: 'unread', label: 'Unread' },
    { value: 'sent', label: 'Sent' },
  ]}
  value={tab}
  onChange={setTab}
/>
```

```tsx
// Icons and a disabled tab.
<Tabs
  tabs={[
    { value: 'day', label: 'Day', icon: <Icon name="sunny" /> },
    { value: 'week', label: 'Week', icon: <Icon name="cloudy" /> },
    { value: 'notes', label: 'Notes', disabled: true },
  ]}
  value={tab}
  onChange={setTab}
  accessibilityLabel="Forecast range"
/>
```

## Variants

| Variant | Layout | Indicator |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `fixed` (default) | Tabs stretch evenly across the width | 2px underline slides between tabs |
| `scrollable` | Tabs size to their content in a horizontal `ScrollView` | Static 2px underline on the active tab — no animation |

## Behavior

- The fixed indicator animates `translateX` on the native driver over
  `motion.durationFast`. It snaps into place on first measure so it never
  slides in from the edge.
- Tab icons receive the resolved color — muted when inactive, `primary` when
  active, subtle when disabled.
- When `testID` is set, each tab appends its `value`, giving test IDs like
  `${testID}-unread`.

## Props

### Tabs props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `tabs` | `TabItem[]` | — | Required. Tab descriptors. |
| `value` | `string` | — | Required. The selected tab's `value`. |
| `onChange` | `(value: string) => void` | — | Required. Called with the newly selected tab's `value`. |
| `variant` | `'fixed' \| 'scrollable'` | `'fixed'` | Layout and indicator behavior. |
| `accessibilityLabel` | `string` | — | Label for the tablist. |
| `style` | `StyleProp<ViewStyle>` | — | Container style overrides. |
| `testID` | `string` | — | Test identifier; each tab appends its `value`. |

### TabItem props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `value` | `string` | — | Required. Stable identifier reported through `onChange`. |
| `label` | `string` | — | Required. Label under the icon. |
| `icon` | `ReactNode` | — | Leading content — icon, anything; `color` is injected when supported. |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | `false` | Disables the tab. |

## Accessibility

The bar is role `tablist`, labelled by `accessibilityLabel`. Each tab is role
`tab` with `accessibilityState` `{ selected, disabled }`, announced by its
`label`. Disabled tabs report `disabled` and ignore presses.
