The kit's typographic primitive — every string on screen renders through it.

import { LinkCard } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';

`Text` is the kit's typographic primitive. Everything that renders text goes
through it so hierarchy, rhythm and font families stay consistent: pick a
`variant` from the theme's type scale instead of setting font sizes by hand,
and let `tone` handle color.

## Import

```tsx
import { Text } from 'react-native-meowui';
```

## Usage

```tsx
<Text variant="display">Account</Text>
<Text variant="body">Your plan renews on March 1.</Text>
<Text variant="caption" tone="error">Card declined.</Text>

<Text variant="label" align="center">CENTERED</Text>

{/* Explicit color wins over tone */}
<Text color="#7C5CFF">Sponsored</Text>

{/* Weight override picks the matching font family */}
<Text weight="600">Highlighted</Text>
```

## Variants

The type scale is a closed set. Sizes step down gently with `600` as the
heaviest weight; `overline` is the only transformed variant.

| Variant | Size | Weight | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `display` | 34 | 600 | Tightest letter spacing. |
| `headline` | 26 | 600 | |
| `title` | 20 | 600 | |
| `subtitle` | 16 | 600 | |
| `bodyLarge` | 17 | 400 | |
| `body` | 15 | 400 | Default variant. |
| `label` | 13 | 500 | |
| `caption` | 12 | 400 | |
| `overline` | 11 | 500 | Uppercase, wide tracking. |
| `mono` | 13 | 400 | Monospace font family. |

## Font families by weight

Each resolved weight maps to a font family from `theme.fonts`. Leave a slot
undefined to fall back to the system font.

| Weight | Font slot |
| --- | --- |
| `400` | `regular` |
| `500` | `medium` |
| `600` | `semibold` |

The effective weight is `weight` if given, otherwise the variant's own
weight, otherwise `400`. Setting `weight` therefore changes both emphasis
and family in one step.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `variant` | `TypographyVariantName` | `'body'` | Typographic variant from the theme's type scale. |
| `tone` | `'primary' \| 'success' \| 'warning' \| 'error' \| 'info' \| 'neutral'` | `'neutral'` | Semantic tone for the text color. Neutral text uses `colors.onSurface`. |
| `color` | `string` | — | Explicit color — wins over `tone`. |
| `align` | `TextStyle['textAlign']` | — | Text alignment. |
| `weight` | `TextStyle['fontWeight']` | — | Override the variant's font weight. |

All other React Native `TextProps` — `style`, `numberOfLines`,
`ellipsizeMode` and so on — pass through unchanged.

## Accessibility

`Text` renders a plain text node, so screen readers announce its content
directly. Keep meaningful text in the tree rather than hiding it behind
decorative `accessibilityLabel` overrides, and reach for variants over
manual font sizes so the visual hierarchy and the announced hierarchy
agree.

Single-line text field with label, helper and error states.

import { LinkCard } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';

TextInput is a single-line text field with a label above, helper text below,
and clear focus and error states. A thin border carries the shape: it turns
primary on focus and error-colored when invalid. The field stays quiet
otherwise — the label sits in place rather than floating, and the background
stays transparent until the field is disabled.

## Import

```tsx
import { TextInput, type TextInputRef } from 'react-native-meowui';
```

## Usage

```tsx
const [email, setEmail] = useState('');

<TextInput
  label="Email"
  value={email}
  onChangeText={setEmail}
  placeholder="you@example.com"
  helperText="We only use this to sign you in."
/>
```

The error state recolors the label, border and helper together, so a single
flag is enough to mark a field invalid.

```tsx
<TextInput
  label="Email"
  value={email}
  onChangeText={setEmail}
  error
  helperText="Enter a valid email address."
/>

<TextInput label="Card number" value="4242 4242 4242 4242" disabled />
```

`leading` and `trailing` render inside the field, around the input — useful
for icons, currency prefixes and units.

```tsx
<TextInput
  label="Price"
  value={price}
  onChangeText={setPrice}
  leading={<Icon name="attach-money" />}
  trailing={<Text>USD</Text>}
/>
```

## Sizes

| Size | Field height | Input font size |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `md` | 44 (from `theme.metrics.input`) | 15 |
| `lg` | 52 (from `theme.metrics.input`) | 16 |

## Props

`TextInputProps` extends React Native's `TextInputProps` (minus `ref`), so the
standard props — `value`, `onChangeText`, `placeholder`, `keyboardType`,
`autoCapitalize`, `maxLength`, and so on — flow through to the native input.
The `style` prop also flows through and styles the input's text.

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `label` | `string` | — | Label rendered above the field. |
| `helperText` | `string` | — | Helper text rendered below the field; uses the error color when `error` is set. |
| `error` | `boolean` | `false` | Marks the field invalid: label, border and helper render in the error color. |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | `false` | Disables editing and mutes the field. |
| `size` | `'md' \| 'lg'` | `'md'` | Field height, resolved through `theme.metrics.input`. |
| `leading` | `ReactNode` | — | Content rendered inside the field, before the input (icons, prefixes). |
| `trailing` | `ReactNode` | — | Content rendered inside the field, after the input (actions, units). |
| `containerStyle` | `StyleProp<ViewStyle>` | — | Style for the outer label / field / helper column. |
| `…RN TextInputProps` | `TextInputProps` | — | Everything else flows through to the native input, including `style` (input text), `onFocus`, `onBlur` and `accessibilityLabel`. |

Two props are intercepted rather than passed straight through:
`placeholderTextColor` defaults to the theme's `onSurfaceSubtle` when omitted,
and `underlineColorAndroid` is forced to transparent so the border stays the
only outline.

## Ref

The ref is a handle to the underlying native input, not the wrapper view.

```tsx
const inputRef = useRef<TextInputRef>(null);

<TextInput ref={inputRef} label="Verification code" />

inputRef.current?.focus();
```

| Method | Signature | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `focus` | `() => void` | Focuses the native input. |
| `blur` | `() => void` | Removes focus. |
| `clear` | `() => void` | Clears the text. |
| `isFocused` | `() => boolean` | Whether the input currently has focus. |
| `setNativeProps` | `(props: Record<string, unknown>) => void` | Sets native props on the underlying input directly. |

The interface is declared structurally instead of re-exporting React Native's
`TextInputInstance`, which aliases a compiler-private class that cannot appear
in emitted declarations.

## Accessibility

The native input keeps React Native's standard text-field semantics. The
visual `label` is a separate `Text`, not programmatically associated with the
input, so pass `accessibilityLabel` (it flows through like any other prop)
when the label text alone is not enough. Focus, error and disabled states are
communicated visually through the border and colors.

App-wide transient notices from a provider-owned queue, stacked from the top and capped at three.

import { LinkCard } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';

Toast is a transient notice you fire from anywhere in the tree.
`ToastProvider` owns the app-wide queue and renders the stack through a
`Portal`, floating above all content; `useToast().show(...)` enqueues a
toast that auto-dismisses on its own. Toasts stack from the top of the
viewport and are capped at three — the oldest drops off when a fourth
arrives. `primary` is intentionally absent from the tone set: toasts speak
in semantics only.

## Import

```tsx
import { ToastProvider, useToast } from 'react-native-meowui';
```

## Usage

Mount the provider once, near the root, inside `MeowProvider`:

```tsx
import { MeowProvider, ToastProvider, useToast } from 'react-native-meowui';

export default function App() {
  return (
    <MeowProvider>
      <ToastProvider>
        <Workspace />
      </ToastProvider>
    </MeowProvider>
  );
}
```

Then call `useToast().show(...)` anywhere below it:

```tsx
function Workspace() {
  const toast = useToast();

  const save = () => {
    toast.show({ message: 'Draft saved', tone: 'success' });
  };

  const remove = () => {
    toast.show({
      message: 'Report deleted',
      tone: 'error',
      duration: 4000,
      action: { label: 'Undo', onPress: restoreReport },
    });
  };

  return (
    <View>
      <Button onPress={save}>Save draft</Button>
      <Button variant="ghost" tone="error" onPress={remove}>Delete</Button>
    </View>
  );
}
```

Calling `useToast()` outside a provider is a no-op, warned about in
development — nothing crashes, but no toast renders.

## The queue

| Behavior | Detail |
| --- | --- |
| Stacking | Toasts stack from the top of the viewport, newest at the bottom of the stack. |
| Cap | Three simultaneous toasts — the oldest drops off when a fourth arrives. |
| Auto-dismiss | Each toast dismisses itself after `duration`, defaulting to 2500ms. |
| Actions | An action's `onPress` runs first, then the toast dismisses. |

Non-neutral tones show an 8dp tone-colored dot before the message, so a
stack of mixed notices stays scannable.

## Props

### ToastProvider

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `children` | `ReactNode` | — | The app tree. Mount the provider once, near the root, inside `MeowProvider`. |

### ToastOptions

Options passed to `useToast().show(...)`.

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `message` | `string` | — | Message body, wrapped at two lines. |
| `tone` | `'neutral' \| 'success' \| 'error' \| 'info' \| 'warning'` | `'neutral'` | Semantic color family. Non-neutral tones show a tone-colored dot. |
| `duration` | `number` | `2500` | Milliseconds before auto-dismiss. |
| `action` | `ToastAction` | — | Trailing action — pressing it runs `onPress` and dismisses the toast. |

`ToastAction` is `{ label, onPress }`.

## Accessibility

Each toast surface carries `accessibilityLiveRegion="polite"`, so screen
readers announce messages as they appear. The action renders with role
`button`, labeled by its `label`.

An icon toggle — radio behavior in a group, boolean flip on its own.

import { LinkCard } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';

`ToggleButton` is an icon toggle. Inside a `ToggleButtonGroup` it behaves
like a radio — exactly one item selected at a time. On its own it flips a
boolean. Either way the selected state is a tonal fill — quiet, not
colorful.

The group is a plain row of square cells; unlike `SegmentedButtons` there
is no border or separator, which suits toolbars.

## Import

```tsx
import { ToggleButton, ToggleButtonGroup } from 'react-native-meowui';
```

## Usage

Standalone — a boolean flip:

```tsx
function Bold() {
  const [bold, setBold] = useState(false);

  return (
    <ToggleButton
      icon={<Icon name="text" />}
      selected={bold}
      onValueChange={setBold}
      accessibilityLabel="Bold"
    />
  );
}
```

Grouped — one of several:

```tsx
function Alignment() {
  const [align, setAlign] = useState<string | null>('left');

  return (
    <ToggleButtonGroup value={align} onValueChange={setAlign}>
      <ToggleButton icon={<Icon name="align-left" />} value="left" />
      <ToggleButton icon={<Icon name="align-center" />} value="center" />
      <ToggleButton icon={<Icon name="align-right" />} value="right" />
    </ToggleButtonGroup>
  );
}
```

Pass `null` as the group's `value` when nothing should be selected.

## Behavior

- A `ToggleButton` counts as "in a group" when it has a `value` and sits
  under a group. Group members ignore their own `selected` prop and
  `onValueChange` callback.
- Pressing a group member selects it; the previous selection is replaced.
  Group selections cannot be toggled off.
- Each cell is 40 by 40 points; icons receive the resolved content color.

## Props

### ToggleButtonGroup

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `value` | `string \| null` | — | The selected item's value, or null when nothing is selected. |
| `onValueChange` | `(value: string) => void` | — | Called with the newly selected value. |
| `children` | `ReactNode` | — | The `ToggleButton`s of the group. |
| `accessibilityLabel` | `string` | — | Label announced for the group. |
| `style` | `StyleProp<ViewStyle>` | — | Track style overrides. |

### ToggleButton

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `icon` | `ReactNode` | — | Icon content; resolved `color` is injected when supported. |
| `value` | `string` | — | Group item identity. Standalone buttons ignore this. |
| `selected` | `boolean` | `false` | Standalone mode: boolean state instead of group membership. |
| `onValueChange` | `(selected: boolean) => void` | — | Standalone mode: called with the next boolean state. |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | `false` | Disables interaction, renders muted. |
| `accessibilityLabel` | `string` | — | Accessible name — required when the icon alone is ambiguous. |
| `style` | `StyleProp<ViewStyle>` | — | Cell style overrides. |
| `testID` | `string` | — | Test identifier. |

## Accessibility

The group renders role `radiogroup`. Group members announce as `radio`
with a `checked` state; standalone buttons announce as `button` with a
`selected` state. Icons carry no meaning to a screen reader, so pass
`accessibilityLabel` on each button.

A long-press hint bubble that anchors to the element it wraps and auto-hides.

import { LinkCard } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';

`Tooltip` wraps a single element and shows a small dark bubble when the
element is long-pressed. The bubble renders through a portal with a
rotated-diamond tail pointing at the child, and hides itself after two
seconds. Tap the bubble to dismiss it early.

## Import

```tsx
import { Tooltip } from 'react-native-meowui';
```

## Usage

Wrap the element — usually a `Pressable`-derivative — and pass the label. No
visibility state is needed; the tooltip manages itself:

```tsx
<Tooltip label="Exports the current report as CSV">
  <Button variant="outline" onPress={exportReport}>
    Export
  </Button>
</Tooltip>

<Tooltip label="Add to favorites" side="bottom">
  <IconButton
    icon={<Icon name="heart" />}
    accessibilityLabel="Add to favorites"
    onPress={favorite}
  />
</Tooltip>
```

## Positioning

The wrapper measures the child with `measureInWindow` and centers the bubble
on it, leaving a 6dp gap. `side` picks which side the bubble appears on —
`'top'` (default) above the child, `'bottom'` below — with the diamond tail
pointing back at it.

## Long-press capture

The wrapper clones the child and replaces its `onLongPress` with the show
handler. The child's own long-press handler is intentionally gone — do not
rely on the wrapped element having one. `onPress` keeps working unchanged.

The bubble is styled with `inverseSurface` and `inverseOnSurface` caption
text, so it reads against any background in both color modes.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `children` | `ReactElement` | — | Single element (usually a `Pressable`-derivative) the tooltip describes. Its `onLongPress` is captured by the wrapper; its `onPress` keeps working. |
| `label` | `string` | — | Text shown in the bubble. |
| `side` | `'top' \| 'bottom'` | `'top'` | Which side of the child the bubble appears on. |
| `style` | `StyleProp<ViewStyle>` | — | Style overrides for the wrapper around the child. |
| `testID` | `string` | — | Test identifier. |

## Accessibility

The bubble is a button that dismisses on tap; the label text is its
accessible content. There is no scrim — the rest of the screen stays
interactive. Because the trigger is a long-press, the wrapped element keeps
its own accessible name and actions; treat the tooltip as a visual hint, not
the only way to learn what a control does.

Accessibility is built into the components rather than bolted on afterwards.
Here is the contract.

## What the kit guarantees

**Roles and states.** Every interactive component sets the right
`accessibilityRole` and `accessibilityState`:

- `Button`, `IconButton`, `FAB`, `Chip` → `button` with `disabled` / `busy` /
  `selected`
- `Checkbox` → `checkbox` with `checked`
- `Radio` → `radio` inside a `radiogroup` container, with `checked`
- `Switch` → `switch` with `checked`
- `Slider` → `adjustable` with `accessibilityValue` (min/max/now) **and**
  `increment` / `decrement` accessibility actions
- `Tabs`, `BottomNavigation` → `tablist` / `tab` with `selected`
- `SegmentedButtons` → `radiogroup` + `radio` (single) or buttons (multi)

**Labels with fallbacks.** Components derive a sensible
`accessibilityLabel` when one exists — `Button` falls back to its string
children, `FAB` to its label, `Avatar` to its label. When the visible content
is ambiguous (an icon-only `IconButton`), passing
`accessibilityLabel` is on you, and the JSDoc says so.

**Overlay semantics.** Portaled overlays are focusable and labeled: dialogs
expose their title, scrims are labeled dismiss buttons, collapsed accordion
content is hidden from the accessibility tree, and the portal overlay frame
itself is transparent to assistive tech so portaled content stays reachable.

**Contrast.** Both reference palettes pair every `on*` content color with its
fill at ≥ 4.5:1 (AA) — including muted variants and the dark theme.

## What stays your responsibility

- **Ambiguous icons** — pass `accessibilityLabel` to icon-only controls.
- **Screen-order context** — announce a toast's meaning if the message alone
  doesn't carry it (`AccessibilityInfo.announceForAccessibility`).
- **Touch targets in your own layouts** — kit controls meet minimum sizes via
  `theme.metrics`; if you shrink them with styles, re-check the 44×44 guideline.
- **Localization** — components accept any string; pluralization and RTL text
  direction are yours. (Layouts use logical properties — `marginStart`,
  `paddingStart` — so RTL mirroring works, but full RTL audit coverage is
  ongoing.)
Use any icon library — or register one renderer for name-based icons.

MeowUI takes a deliberate position on icons: **the kit ships none**. Icon
fonts and SVG packs are an app-level concern, and bundling one would force a
dependency on every consumer.

## Pass any element

Every `icon` prop accepts a `ReactNode`. This is the primary API and works
with anything — `@expo/vector-icons`, `react-native-vector-icons`, SVG via
`react-native-svg`, an image, emoji:

```tsx
import Ionicons from '@expo/vector-icons/Ionicons';

<Button icon={<Ionicons name="save" color="white" />}>Save</Button>
<IconButton icon={<Ionicons name="settings" />} accessibilityLabel="Settings" />
```

Components that set color contextually — `Button`, `IconButton`, `FAB`,
`Tabs`, list rows — **clone the icon element and inject the resolved
`color` (and `size`) when the element supports those props and hasn't set its
own**. That's why the `Button` example above renders white-on-primary without
hardcoding, and why a custom SVG still works if it ignores the injected props.

## The Icon adapter

If you prefer name-based icons across the whole kit, register a renderer once
at startup. `react-native-vector-icons` and `@expo/vector-icons` families
satisfy the contract as-is:

```tsx
// index.js / App.tsx — before anything renders
import Ionicons from '@expo/vector-icons/Ionicons';
import { setIconRenderer } from 'react-native-meowui';

setIconRenderer(Ionicons);
```

```tsx
import { Icon } from 'react-native-meowui';

<Icon name="checkmark-circle" size={20} color="#2E7D4F" />
```

- `color` defaults to `theme.colors.onSurface`.
- Without a registered renderer, `<Icon>` renders nothing (with a dev-mode
  warning) — safe fallback, never a crash.
- Components that take `ReactNode` icons are unaffected either way.

## Built-in glyphs

A few components draw their own tiny glyphs from `View`s instead of an icon
font — the checkmark on a selected `Chip`, the close ✕ on an input chip, the
chevrons in `Appbar.BackAction`, `Menu`'s selected check,
`DataTablePagination`'s pager, `Searchbar`'s magnifier and clear button. This
keeps those components functional with **zero icon setup**; pass `icon` props
to replace them with your own.
How Dialog, Menu, BottomSheet, Toast and friends escape the view tree.

Floating UI has a classic React Native problem: a menu inside a card inside a
`ScrollView` gets clipped, stacked, or transformed away by its ancestors.
MeowUI solves this once, in one place.

## Portal and PortalHost

`<Portal>` teleports its children to the nearest `<PortalHost>` **above the
surrounding tree**:

```tsx
import { Portal, PortalHost, Surface } from 'react-native-meowui';

<PortalHost>
  <Text>I render in place</Text>
  <Portal>
    <Surface style={{ position: 'absolute', bottom: 24, left: 24 }}>
      I render in the host's overlay, above everything
    </Surface>
  </Portal>
</PortalHost>
```

Portaled content keeps rendering and re-rendering normally — only its position
in the hierarchy changes. Component instances are preserved across re-renders,
so state inside a portal is not lost.

`MeowProvider` already includes a `PortalHost`, so most apps mount none
explicitly. Nest additional hosts when content must layer inside a region
(e.g. a portal that stays inside a modal).

## Stacking by token, not by luck

Every kit overlay passes its `theme.zIndex` token when it portals, and the
host sorts entries by it:

| Layer | Token | Value |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Menus & Select dropdowns | `zIndex.menu` | 900 |
| Bottom sheets | `zIndex.sheet` | 950 |
| Dialogs & Modal | `zIndex.dialog` | 1000 |
| Toasts & snackbars | `zIndex.toast` | 1050 |
| Tooltips | `zIndex.tooltip` | 1100 |

A Dialog opened *after* a Toast still renders **below** it — stacking follows
the tokens, not mount order. For your own portaled content, pass a zIndex:

```tsx
<Portal zIndex={925}>{/* above menus, below sheets */}</Portal>
```

## Which overlay to use

| Need | Component |
| --- | --- |
| A decision the user must make | `Dialog` / `AlertDialog` |
| A secondary surface with actions | `BottomSheet` |
| A list of actions anchored to a trigger | `Menu` |
| Passive, non-blocking message | `Snackbar` / `Toast` |
| Full custom layout | `Modal` |
| A label on long-press | `Tooltip` |

All of them animate entrances with native-driver transforms and fade their
scrim; see each component's page for specifics.

How MeowUI stays fast — architecture decisions and what they cost.

MeowUI is built so that speed is a property of the architecture, not an
optimization pass. The decisions below are visible in the source and easy to
verify in a profile.

## Zero runtime dependencies

The package contains no runtime dependencies at all. Everything is built on
React Native primitives: `View`, `Text`, `Pressable`, `Animated`, `PanResponder`.

Concretely, this means:

- **No Reanimated / Gesture Handler** — no worklet runtime to boot, no Babel
  plugin, no `react-native-gesture-handler` wrapper components, no library-level
  JS thread work per frame.
- **No Expo modules** — no `expo-blur`, `expo-linear-gradient`, or
  `masked-view` transitively pulled into bare RN apps.
- **Smaller install and bundle.** One package, no transitive library graph.

## Native-driver animations only

All motion — press feedback, overlay entrances, switch thumbs, the Tabs
indicator, FAB stacks — uses RN's built-in `Animated` with `useNativeDriver:
true` for opacity and transform. The JS thread is not involved per frame.

The two documented exceptions are deliberate:

- **Measured-height expansions** (`Collapsible`, `ListAccordion` bodies) animate
  height on the JS driver — height is not a native-driveable property, and the
  trees being expanded are small.
- **Determinate `ProgressBar`** animates a measured width. The indeterminate
  mode uses a native-driven transform loop.

## Render architecture

- **Frozen theme objects.** `createTheme()` output is `Object.freeze`d; a
  theme's identity changes only when the mode or overrides actually change, so
  `React.memo` boundaries hold.
- **Split contexts.** The theme and the mode controller (`setMode`, `toggleMode`)
  live in separate contexts. Components subscribed to `useTheme()` never
  re-render because of controller identity churn.
- **Memoized components.** Every public component is wrapped in `React.memo`.
- **Hoisted styles.** Static styles are `StyleSheet.create`d at module scope;
  theme-driven values are plain inline objects (cheap for the stylesheet
  runtime, no cache machinery).

## Press feedback without springs

Interaction is communicated with a background tint or opacity dip on
`Pressable` — no scale springs, no bounces. This is a design decision as much
as a performance one: it reads calmer and costs nothing.

## What this buys you in practice

A screen full of MeowUI components boots with zero additional native modules,
zero Babel transforms, and no per-frame library work. On low-end Android
devices this is usually the difference between "library demo" and "app-ready".

How MeowUI development works and the conventions every component follows.

MeowUI's quality comes from one rule: **the kit must feel designed by a single
person.** The conventions below exist to enforce that.

## Principles

1. **Zero runtime dependencies.** Only `react` and `react-native` are peers.
   Use RN's built-in `Animated` (native driver for opacity/transform) and
   `Pressable`.
2. **Calm, professional visual language.** Hairline borders over heavy shadows,
   small radii, one restrained accent, muted semantic colors, quiet motion.
3. **Structure over decoration.** Color comes from the theme, never hardcoded.
   If you're adding a hex value to a component, add a token instead.
4. **Speed is a feature.** Memoize components, hoist static styles, don't
   subscribe more of the tree than needed.

## Component conventions

The full spec lives in [CONTRIBUTING.md](https://github.com/heymeowcat/react-native-meowui/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md)
in the repository. The short version:

- One component per folder: `src/components/<Name>/<Name>.tsx` + `index.ts`.
- Props interface exported as `<Name>Props`; sizes `'sm' | 'md' | 'lg'` via
  `theme.metrics`; intent via the `Tone` union via `theme.colors`.
- Strict TypeScript with `import type`; `React.memo` on every component.
- JSDoc on every public component and non-obvious prop — these docs pages are
  written from those contracts.
- Accessibility roles and states threaded through interactive components.

Follow the OS, force a mode, or control it yourself.

## Follow the OS (default)

With no props, `MeowProvider` tracks the system color scheme:

```tsx
<MeowProvider>{children}</MeowProvider>
```

## Force a mode

```tsx
<MeowProvider mode="dark">{children}</MeowProvider>
<MeowProvider mode="light">{children}</MeowProvider>
```

## Switch at runtime

The uncontrolled provider manages a preference (`'light' | 'dark' | 'system'`)
internally and exposes it through `useThemeController`:

```tsx
import { Button, useThemeController } from 'react-native-meowui';

function ThemeToggle() {
  const { mode, setMode, toggleMode } = useThemeController();

  return (
    <>
      <Button variant="ghost" onPress={toggleMode}>
        {mode === 'dark' ? 'Light' : 'Dark'} mode
      </Button>
      <Button variant="ghost" onPress={() => setMode('system')}>
        Use system
      </Button>
    </>
  );
}
```

Hook `onModeChange` to persist the preference or fire analytics:

```tsx
<MeowProvider onModeChange={(mode) => storage.set('theme', mode)}>
  {children}
</MeowProvider>
```

## Controlled

If the mode lives in your own state (Redux, MMKV, a settings screen), build the
theme yourself and pass it — the provider renders exactly what it receives:

```tsx
import { createTheme, MeowProvider } from 'react-native-meowui';

function Root() {
  const mode = useAppThemeMode(); // your store
  const theme = useMemo(() => createTheme({ mode, ...overrides }), [mode]);

  return <MeowProvider theme={theme}>{children}</MeowProvider>;
}
```

## How dark mode differs

The dark palette is not an inversion — it is tuned separately:

- Surfaces lift by brightness (`#0F1317 → #161B21 → #1E242B`) instead of
  shadow, so elevation reads on OLED and LCD alike.
- Accent and semantic colors are lightened (`primary` `#336699` → `#7FA8D9`)
  to keep AA contrast on dark fills, with dark `on*` colors.
- The scrim deepens (`rgba(0,0,0,0.6)`), and `inverseSurface` flips to a light
  value so snackbars and tooltips stay high-contrast.

See the full values in [Color tokens](/theming/colors/#dark-slate-not-black).
How MeowUI's token system works and the grammar behind it.

MeowUI is themed entirely through **semantic tokens**. Components never contain
hex values — if you can't achieve a look through tokens, that's considered a
bug in the token system, not a reason to reach for inline overrides.

## The color grammar

Every color token follows a strict naming rule, so intent is always readable
in both the theme and your own styles:

| Prefix | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `surface*` | Background fills. `background` is the page canvas, `surface` sits on it (cards, bars, sheets), `surfaceMuted` is a secondary fill, `surfaceActive` a pressed fill. |
| `on*` | Content rendered **on top of** the matching fill. `onSurface` pairs with `surface`, `onPrimary` with `primary`. |
| `*Muted` | A soft, low-chroma fill for tonal variants (`primaryMuted`), with its own `onPrimaryMuted` content color. |
| `outline` / `outlineStrong` | Hairline borders; strong is for inputs and emphasized edges. |
| `inverseSurface` / `inverseOnSurface` | The high-contrast pairing for overlays: snackbars, toasts, tooltips. |

Plus five **tones** — `primary`, `success`, `warning`, `error`, `info` — each
with solid, on-solid, muted and on-muted variants. The `Tone` union flows into
component props (`tone="error"`), so you never pass raw colors to express
intent.

## Motion

Motion is felt, not seen — quick, decelerating, never bouncy.

| Token | Value | Used for |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `durationFast` | 120 ms | presses, chevrons, menu entrance |
| `durationBase` | 180 ms | switches, tabs indicator, FAB stack |
| `durationSlow` | 260 ms | large content moves |
| `durationOverlay` | 220 ms | dialogs, sheets, snackbars |

Easing curves are fixed in `theme/motion` (`easingStandard`, `easingExit`) and
intentionally not themeable — durations are yours to tune, curves are the
kit's voice.
